title: Software Engineer
description: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The LS-SWIFT division delivers high-throughput patterned wafer inspection systems that support advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its mission is to provide industry-leading defect detection with optimal cost of ownership across a wide range of applications. LS systems enable precise, cost-effective inspection for cutting-edge process nodes, while SWIFT systems offer comprehensive macro inspection of all wafer surfaces—capabilities that are especially critical for advanced packaging, as well as logic, memory, and automotive applications. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Company Overview KLA is a global leader in diversified electronics for the semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem. Virtually every electronic device in the world is produced using our technologies. No laptop, smartphone, wearable device, voice-controlled gadget, flexible screen, VR device or smart car would have made it into your hands without us. KLA invents systems and solutions for the manufacturing of wafers and reticles, integrated circuits, packaging, printed circuit boards and flat panel displays. The innovative ideas and devices that are advancing humanity all begin with inspiration, research and development. KLA focuses more than average on innovation and we invest 15% of sales back into R&D. Our expert teams of physicists, engineers, data scientists and problem-solvers work together with the world’s leading technology providers to accelerate the delivery of tomorrow’s electronic devices. Life here is exciting and our teams thrive on tackling really hard problems. There is never a dull moment with us. Group/Division With over 40 years of semiconductor process control experience, chipmakers around the globe rely on KLA to ensure that their fabs ramp next-generation devices to volume production quickly and cost-effectively. Enabling the movement towards advanced chip design, KLA's Global Products Group (GPG), which is responsible for creating all of KLA’s metrology and inspection products, is looking for the best and the brightest research scientist, software engineers, application development engineers, and senior product technology process engineers. The LS-SWIFT Division of KLA’s Global Products Group provides patterned wafer inspection systems for high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. Its mission is to deliver market-leading cost of ownership in defect detection for a broad range of applications in the production of semiconductors. Customers from the foundry, logic, memory, automotive, MEMS, advanced packaging and other markets rely upon high-sample wafer inspection information generated by LS-SWIFT products. LS (Laser Scanning) systems enable cost-effective patterned wafer defect detection for the industry’s most sophisticated process technologies deployed in leading-edge foundry, logic, DRAM, and NAND fabs. SWIFT (Simultaneous Wafer Inspection at Fast Throughput) systems deliver all-wafer-surface (frontside, backside, and edge) macro inspection that is critical for automotive IC, MEMS, and advanced packaging processes as well as foundry/logic and memory fabs. LS-SWIFT operates from a global footprint that includes the US, Singapore, India and Germany, and serves a worldwide customer base across Asia, Europe and North America. Design skills is a plus. Good analytical and problem-solving abilities Thorough knowledge of SDLC and software engineering Strong verbal and written communication and team-work skills Ability to develop Software with Clean Code and SOLID principles Minimum Qualifications Master's Level Degree Bachelor's Level Degree and related work experience of 2+years Minimum Qualifications Master's Level Degree or work experience of 0 years , Bachelor's Level Degree or work experience of 1 years About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. description: JD-Senior-AI-Software-Engineer Senior — Job Description - Position Details Job Title Senior AI Software Engineer – Application Modernisation Experience 4–7 years in software development, including at least 12 months of sustained, hands-on use of an agentic AI coding tool on real applications (see Required Skills) Openings 1 Employment Type Full-time Department Engineering — Product Development Location Chennai (in-office) About ColorPodge ColorPodge develops cloud-based colour-management software for the apparel and homewares industries. Its SaaS products support colour development, approvals, supply-chain collaboration, and specialised business processes for international customers. Role Summary ColorPodge is changing the way it builds and maintains software. AI coding agents such as Claude Code are now part of everyday development: we use them to understand established applications, upgrade them to current frameworks while they remain in use, reconstruct smaller legacy applications on a modern stack, and build new products. We are looking for an engineer who already works this way. You will have used AI coding tools to build, modernise, debug or maintain real applications, not only to generate snippets, and you will be able to take an unfamiliar application, with its code, its database and its business rules, and deliver a modernised or reconstructed version with evidence that it behaves correctly. The work ranges from upgrading established, business-critical web applications to current framework, language and database versions while they stay in use, with their features, data and user workflows preserved, to reconstructing legacy applications as new builds and building new modules on PHP 8 and modern JavaScript. The role is hands-on and outcome-owned: you direct the tools, you review and verify what they produce, and you are the author of record for everything that is merged. Key Responsibilities AI-assisted analysis and modernisation • • • • Use AI coding tools to map an unfamiliar application: its modules, URL map, data model, business rules, role-based behaviour and integrations; produce written findings that others can check. Plan and carry out modernisation module by module with the Tech Lead: upgrade in place (framework, language and database versions) or reconstruct on a modern stack, as agreed per module. Preserve existing URLs, form and API contracts, calculations, workflow outcomes and emails wherever the application stays in use; document and agree any deliberate change in behaviour before it is made. Direct the tools with precise specifications, constraints and acceptance criteria; break work into small verifiable steps; keep the tools within the agreed scope (production systems and customer data stay out of their reach). Verification and quality • • • • Review every AI-generated change as its author: read it, run it, and check its logic, data handling, security and performance before it is merged. Generate and maintain automated tests (PHPUnit for services and models; Playwright or similar for pages, in a real browser) and use them as the proof that behaviour is unchanged and as the regression suite; write tests first where none exist. Compare old and new behaviour per user role with evidence: the same controls, data, validations, database writes and emails. Debug failures independently, including failures in the tool's own output: invented APIs, silently changed behaviour, insecure shortcuts, and tests that pass without testing anything. Engineering practice Develop in PHP 8, MySQL 8, JavaScript, HTML and CSS using a modern application structure: explicit routes, controllers, models, services for business logic, filters or middleware for authentication and security, migrations with working rollback, and configuration through environment variables. Apply secure coding practices (input validation, output escaping, CSRF protection, role-based authorisation, secure file handling) and fix weaknesses found in existing code. Follow the Git workflow: feature branches, small reviewable commits, pull requests and code review, including review of colleagues' AI-assisted changes. Work in containerised development and staging environments; deploy, verify and investigate issues from application and server logs; respect the safety rules for non-production environments (no real email, no production credentials, isolated test data). Improve the user interface progressively while modernising (forms, tables, dialogs, responsiveness, accessibility) without removing features or changing navigation. Collaboration and reporting Work to a module-by-module plan, report progress against milestones with evidence, and raise risks and blockers early. Clarify ambiguous legacy behaviour with the Tech Lead and business stakeholders before reproducing or changing it. Document the modules delivered: structure, decisions taken, agreed changes in behaviour, and what the support team needs to know. Share effective prompts, workflows, guardrails and lessons with the team, and help colleagues adopt AI assisted development well. Use only company-approved AI tools and accounts, and follow the rules on what code and data may be sent to them. Required Skills and Qualifications Practical AI-assisted development experience (mandatory). At least 12 months of sustained, hands-on use of an agentic AI coding tool (Claude Code, or a comparable tool such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot in agent mode, OpenAI Codex CLI, Windsurf or Aider) to build, modernise, debug or maintain real applications. Occasional code generation in a chat window does not qualify. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to show this work and will complete a practical assessment in which they use an AI tool to understand and modify an unfamiliar application. Professional experience developing and maintaining production web applications, owning features from analysis to release. Experience modernising, migrating or reconstructing a legacy application (a framework or language major-version upgrade, a re-platforming or a rebuild) while the original stayed in use. Ability to read unfamiliar code and database schemas, work out what they do and why, and extract the business rules from them. Strong PHP (8.x: type declarations, null handling, exceptions, namespaces, Composer, PSR standards) and MySQL (schema design, joins, indexes, query optimisation, transactions, version differences); solid JavaScript, HTML and CSS, including AJAX-driven pages. Experience writing and maintaining automated tests (PHPUnit; Playwright, Cypress or Selenium) and working with a regression suite. Ability to review, debug and validate AI-generated code independently: spotting incorrect logic, insecure patterns, performance problems and tests that prove nothing. Understanding of application security (authentication, session handling, role-based authorisation, CSRF, XSS, SQL injection, secure file handling), performance, and deployment (Linux, Nginx or Apache, PHP-FPM, Docker, Git). Disciplined, evidence-based working style: small verifiable changes, proof before claiming a module is complete, and clear written communication. Preferred Skills CodeIgniter 3 and 4, or Laravel; experience with a framework or PHP major-version upgrade. Experience setting up AI coding agents for a team: project instruction files, tool permissions and guardrails, MCP integrations, test-driven loops, or running several agents in parallel. Role-based business applications in supply chain, retail, manufacturing or approval workflows. Cloud platforms (Azure or AWS), CI/CD pipelines, cloud storage, transactional email services and single sign-on integrations. Education Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant certifications are a plus. ISMS / ISO/IEC 27001 Responsibilities Practice good cyber hygiene by following the established policies and procedures: Keep your devices and applications patched and up to date. Use strong, unique passphrases — make them long, complex, or both. Secure all devices with a strong password or PIN, and set them to lock after a few minutes of inactivity as per IT policy. Encrypt anything that stores sensitive information. Turn on built-in anti-malware software and firewall. Back up important files and data. Use separate accounts for privileged (administrator) and non-privileged (user) access. Complete required cybersecurity training. Report security incidents and respond to security notices. Refrain from sharing or discussing company information with external parties both during and after your employment. Pay: ₹800,000.00 - ₹1,200,000.00 per year Benefits: Provident Fund Work Location: In person

description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright TypeScript pytest Python FastAPI PostgreSQL SQL REST OpenAPI GitHub Actions Docker HL7 v2 FHIR ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover
